newsitem.title: USA: Andrews Group to buy more Toy Biz shares.
newsitem.headline: Andrews Group to buy more Toy Biz shares.

text.p: Andrews Group Inc said Thursday it agreed to buy about 67 percent of Toy Biz Inc's class A common at a price per share consisting of cash and Andrews debt estimated to have a value below current market.

It said the purchase from Isaac Perlmutter and Avi Arad, members of Toy Biz management, is conditioned on Andrews Group buying additional Marvel Entertainment Group Inc equity. Andrews noted Mavel holds substantially all of Toy Biz's Class B common.
Andrews Group said it also anticipates Marvel will propose acquiring all remaining Toy Biz shares.
The Marvel offer would be at a cash price approximating the current market, Andrews Group said.
The stock closed today at 19-1/8, up 3/8.

It said Toy Biz would become a wholly owned Marvel subsidiary with Joseph M. Ahearn continuing as president and chief executive officer and Arad and Perlmutter retaining their Toy Biz management responsibilities.
The Marvel proposal to Toy Biz will also be conditioned on Andrews Group purchasing new Marvel equity, Andrews said, adding it and Marvel could waive these conditions.
Andrews Group and other entities controlled by investor Ron Perlman now own 80 percent of Marvel's equity.

In anticipation of receiving a proposal, Toy Biz directors have formed a special committee of directors not affiliated with Andrews Group or Marvel to negotiate with Marvel on behalf of the Toy Biz minority stockholders.

Andrews Group said the proposal it expects to make to purchase new Marvel equity will be subject to a number of significant conditions, including a waiver of covenants contained in its bank credit facilities, the restructuring of those facilities to provide for Marvel's cash requirements; and an agreement among Marvel, its banks, the holders of certain Marvel holding company bonds and Andrews Group on the terms of the Andrews Group purchase.

Andrews Group pointed out that any such purchase would result in substantial dilution to the existing Marvel shares, including the Marvel shares which serve as collateral for Marvel holding company bonds.
